title: 3rd Stopping Place 3rd Truth Applying The Spring Army And The Travelers Judgment On Resurrection

questions.question: After thinking about one spring as a sign, what conclusion did the traveler reach about denying resurrection?
questions.answer: He concluded that rejecting resurrection deserves punishment because it rejects clear proofs, divine promises, and divine power.

questions.question: According to the passage, why is denial of resurrection a serious mistake?
questions.answer: Because it means refusing to accept many promises and doubting the ability of the One who has full power to bring it about.

questions.question: Whose repeated assurances are mentioned as support for resurrection?
questions.answer: The assurances brought through all of the prophets are mentioned.

questions.question: Besides the prophets, what other source is given as repeated evidence for resurrection?
questions.answer: Many verses of the Qur’an, both direct and indirect, are given as evidence.

questions.question: How often does the passage say these assurances were given?
questions.answer: It says they were given many times, described as thousands of times.

questions.question: How is the future resurrection compared with what happens in spring?
questions.answer: It is presented as easier than the many amazing gatherings and renewals that appear every spring.

questions.question: What quality of Allah is emphasized to answer doubts about resurrection?
questions.answer: His irresistible and complete power is emphasized.

questions.question: What other divine quality is stressed alongside power?
questions.answer: Majestic wrath and glory are also stressed, showing that justice is part of the matter.

questions.question: What response came from the nafs after the traveler’s reflection?
questions.answer: It accepted the statement and expressed belief in it.

questions.question: What is the main subject of the traveler’s inner reflection in this passage?
questions.answer: It is the justice of punishment for those who deny resurrection.

questions.question: On what basis does the traveler call that punishment just?
questions.answer: He sees it as just because denial rejects repeated divine promises and denies divine ability.

questions.question: What two kinds of testimony are mentioned in support of resurrection?
questions.answer: The message of the prophets and the verses of the Qur’an.

questions.question: Does the passage present resurrection as difficult or easy for Allah? Explain.
questions.answer: It presents it as easy for Allah, even easier than the repeated wonders seen in spring.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention spring more than once?
questions.answer: To use visible, repeated events in nature as evidence that bringing life back is fully possible.

questions.question: What role do the Qur’anic verses play in the traveler’s reasoning?
questions.answer: They serve as repeated revealed proof that resurrection and gathering will happen.

questions.question: What is significant about the nafs answering back?
questions.answer: It shows an inner struggle ending in submission to the truth.

questions.question: What final attitude is reached by the end of the passage?
questions.answer: An attitude of acceptance and belief.

questions.question: What judgment does he make about people who deny resurrection?
questions.answer: He judges that punishment in Hell is deserved for them.

questions.question: What is one reason he gives for that judgment related to Allah’s words?
questions.answer: Denial goes against many promises given by Allah.

questions.question: What is another reason he gives related to Allah’s ability?
questions.answer: Denial also means refusing to accept the power of the One who can certainly do it.

questions.question: Which messengers are said to have received this promise?
questions.answer: All of the prophets are described as having been assured of it.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an support this teaching according to the passage?
questions.answer: It contains many verses that state or indicate resurrection and gathering.

questions.question: What comparison is made between the final resurrection and springtime events?
questions.answer: The final resurrection is said to be easier than the many extraordinary renewals that happen every spring.

questions.question: What does the inner self say in reply?
questions.answer: It says that it believes what was said.

questions.question: How does that reply complete the passage?
questions.answer: It shows the argument moved from reflection to inward approval.

questions.question: What central belief is defended in this passage?
questions.answer: The belief that resurrection and the final gathering will truly happen.

questions.question: What moral consequence is linked to rejecting that belief?
questions.answer: Such rejection is linked to deserving punishment.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does denial of resurrection amount to regarding divine promises?
questions.answer: It amounts to calling those promises false or refusing to accept them.

questions.question: According to the passage, what does denial of resurrection amount to regarding divine power?
questions.answer: It amounts to denying the power of Allah to bring people back to life.

questions.question: How broad is the prophetic witness described here?
questions.answer: It includes every prophet.

questions.question: How broad is the Qur’anic witness described here?
questions.answer: It includes many verses, some plain in meaning and others pointing by indication.

questions.question: What natural example is used to make resurrection easier to understand?
questions.answer: The repeated renewal and gathering seen in spring.

questions.question: What does the passage teach about Allah’s power by using spring as evidence?
questions.answer: It teaches that His power is so great that raising the dead is not hard for Him.

questions.question: How is the final resurrection ranked in relation to spring renewals?
questions.answer: It is described as easier than those repeated spring wonders.

questions.question: What change happens in the traveler’s inner conversation by the end?
questions.answer: Doubt is replaced by belief and agreement.

questions.question: In this passage, what does the traveler say is completely fair for deniers of resurrection?
questions.answer: He says the punishment of Hell is completely fair for them.

questions.question: What first reason does he give for calling it fair?
questions.answer: They reject many divine promises.

questions.question: What second reason does he give?
questions.answer: They deny the ability of the One who has overwhelming power.

questions.question: What description of Allah strengthens the warning in the passage?
questions.answer: Allah is described with power, majesty, and wrath.

questions.question: Who are said to have received repeated promises about resurrection?
questions.answer: The prophets all received those promises.

questions.question: How does the Qur’an reinforce the same message?
questions.answer: It confirms resurrection in many verses through clear statements and meaningful indications.

questions.question: Why does the passage bring in the example of spring?
questions.answer: To show a visible pattern of life being brought forth again and gathered in amazing ways.

questions.question: If spring renewals happen again and again, what conclusion does the traveler draw about the final resurrection?
questions.answer: He concludes that the final resurrection is certainly within divine power and even easier.

questions.question: What kind of reasoning is used here: emotional only, textual only, or both revealed and observed?
questions.answer: It uses both revealed proof and observed signs.

questions.question: How does the nafs respond to this reasoning?
questions.answer: It responds with belief and acceptance.

questions.question: What event or doctrine is at the center of the passage?
questions.answer: The resurrection and the gathering after it.

questions.question: How does the traveler evaluate disbelief in that doctrine?
questions.answer: He sees it as a grave wrong that justly leads to punishment.

questions.question: What revealed source connected to all messengers is used as evidence?
questions.answer: The repeated promise conveyed through all the prophets.

questions.question: What revealed written source is also used as evidence?
questions.answer: The Qur’an, through many verses.

questions.question: In what two ways do those verses support the belief?
questions.answer: Some speak about it plainly, and others point to it indirectly.

questions.question: What attribute of Allah answers the claim that resurrection cannot happen?
questions.answer: His absolute power answers that claim.

questions.question: What example from the world is used to help explain the possibility of resurrection?
questions.answer: The repeated reviving and organizing seen every spring.

questions.question: How does the passage compare the final gathering with springtime revivals?
questions.answer: It says the final gathering is easier than those many spring revivals.

questions.question: What does the traveler’s conversation with his nafs reveal about faith?
questions.answer: Faith involves addressing the inner self and bringing it to accept clear evidence.

questions.question: What is the final result of the inner dialogue?
questions.answer: The inner self confirms belief.
